subject: Staged decommitment & conditional downsize language for LumenPath POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Legal <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged decommitment & conditional downsize language for LumenPath POC

Team — looping you in for a quick exec sign-off on a non-standard early-termination/downsize ask from LumenPath. Details below and attached is the customer's redline (lumenpath_redline_v1.docx). High level:

- Account: LumenPath Health (POC + 12-month committed capacity)
- Ask: ability to downsize committed capacity after go-live with a staged ramp and an early-exit credit; customer requests price-protection for 6 months post-downsize.
- Customer proposed terms (from procurement): 120-day pilot stability, then a 120-day window during which they can downsize to as low as 50% of committed capacity with a 25% one-time early-exit credit and 60-day notice.

Impact/ask for approvals:
- They're requesting a 25% early-exit credit against remaining committed spend — revenue impact approx $45k in first-year ARR if granted.
- We should consider a capped credit or tie it to usage thresholds (e.g., <60% of committed usage).
- They also want a 6-month pricing protection for the reduced band.

Requesting:
1) Deal desk / revenue approval for a maximum 20% one-time early-exit credit (or approval to go to 25% if legal signs off the tighter usage thresholds).
2) Legal to sign-off language for staged ramp and notice window that preserves Redwood's right to midterm repricing if usage falls under thresholds.

Next steps: Karthik — can you run revenue math and advise on acceptable credit cap? Laura — please draft the conditional downsize clause we can attach. Vivek — can you provide a quick executive steer on whether we accept a 120-day decommitment window or push to 90 days?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged decommitment & conditional downsize language for LumenPath POC

Marissa — thanks for the summary and redline. A few clarifying Qs and my initial take: 

1) The customer-proposed 25% credit is on remaining committed spend, correct? Need to confirm whether they expect pro rata application across billing months or a lump-sum credit.
2) The requested 120-day window post-go-live to downsize to 50% is fairly generous. Alternative: we can offer a three-stage ramp-down over 120 days (75% for 30 days, 60% for the next 60 days, then 50%) with a scaled credit (20% / 12% / 6%). That reduces upfront hit and ties credits to timing.
3) Price protection: we can lock pricing for 90 days post-downsize instead of 180 unless they buy a lightweight renewal protection add-on.

Revenue math (rough): at proposed committed ARR of $225k, a 25% credit on remaining year is ~ $56k (if mid-year). With staged scaled credit proposal, expected impact closer to $30–35k. If we cap at 20% in a single credit, impact ~ $45k.

My recommendation: approve up to 20% one-time credit as default; allow escalation to 25% only if legal embeds a usage-threshold clause (e.g., credit only triggers if trailing 30-day usage <50% of committed). Ask finance to flag for revenue recognition impact.

If we get Vivek to sign off, Laura, can you draft the staged ramp clause and the usage threshold language? Marissa — please reply with confirmation you can accept the scaled ramp approach from the customer side.

—Karthik
Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@lumenpath.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lumenpath.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged decommitment & conditional downsize language for LumenPath POC

Hi Marissa / team — thanks for pulling this together. A few clarifications from procurement so we have a workable path forward internally: 

- We need the ability to downsize if the POC doesn't meet scalability goals — LumenPath's internal leadership requires a formal decommitment path that lets us reduce committed spend to 50% within 120 days post-go-live.
- The 25% early-exit credit was requested to offset migration/ops costs if we downsize early; we would accept a staged credit tied to ramp timing but prefer a higher upfront credit (25%) for predictability.
- Price protection for the reduced band is important — we cannot face price increases for 6 months after downsize; if Redwood offers 3 months we'll consider a longer notice window.

We're happy to accept a staged ramp if it preserves a meaningful credit earlier in the window. Attached is our internal procurement PO for reference (lumenpath_po_78421.pdf). Our procurement lead is available for a 30-min call to resolve the last bits.

Would Redwood be open to the following concession to bridge the gap?

- 25% early-exit credit, but credit only triggers if trailing 30-day usage is <55% of committed baseline.
- 60-day notice to implement downsize (so we can reallocate capacity).
- 120-day total eligibility window post-go-live.

If we can lock that in we'll sign the SOW and move to procurement.

Thanks,
Sara Mills
Director, Infrastructure Programs | LumenPath Health
sara.mills@lumenpath.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged decommitment & conditional downsize language for LumenPath POC

Thanks everyone — read the thread and ran numbers with finance. Executive steer below: 

1) Approval: we will approve a conditional program that allows a staged downsize up to 50% within a 120-day window post-go-live, provided we get the following protections in contract language: 
   - The early-exit credit will be capped at 20% as our standard, but we will allow up to 25% only if the trigger is validated by a usage-threshold (trailing 30-day usage <55% of committed baseline) and finance signs off on revenue treatment.
   - A 60-day implementation notice is acceptable.
   - Pricing protection for the reduced band will be 90 days; if customer wants 180 days, they must take the renewal-price-protection add-on (standard charge).

2) Conditions: Legal (Laura) to add a clause that clearly defines: trigger metric, measurement window, notice mechanics, and a cap on cumulative credits across the term. Also require the customer to commit to a migration plan if they downsize (so we can free GPU capacity).

3) Execution: Marissa — please confirm with the customer that they accept the conditional threshold approach (20% base credit, up to 25% if usage <55% + finance approval). Karthik — please prepare the revenue-impact memo for finance and tag the deal so revenue ops can set a manual recognition flag. Laura — please attach the clause to the SOW and push for final sign-off.

I'll sign off formally once legal attaches the language and finance confirms revenue treatment. Keep me posted.

—Vivek
Head of Revenue | Redwood Inference
